title: Umbrella: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes — hangs/timeouts (kernel + scheduling)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
## Why this exists
We are seeing customer-visible timeouts/5xx and oncall load driven by multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) worker groups entering a stuck state under sustained load (high concurrency + long-running streams). Current symptoms strongly suggest a combination of (1) collective async errors not surfacing promptly, (2) scheduler/barrier + cancellation interactions that can deadlock a TP group, (3) lack of a TP-group health model/circuit breaker, and (4) insufficient observability to quickly classify the stall (kernel vs comm vs scheduler starvation).

This umbrella tracks the end-to-end initiative: triage → fixes → validation → canary/rollout.

---

## Goals (what “done” means)
1) **Eliminate known TP hang signatures** under the repro suite + representative prod traffic patterns.
2) **Reduce customer-visible failures** attributable to TP hangs:
   - ↓ request timeouts / 5xx in large Hosted pools and Dedicated clusters with TP enabled
   - ↓ incident frequency and MTTR for TP-related events
3) **Make failures fail-fast and self-contained**:
   - stuck TP groups are detected via watchdog
   - groups are quarantined (no new work)
   - controlled teardown/reset, with explicit metrics and clear error propagation
4) **Provide oncall-grade observability** to distinguish:
   - comm stall (collectives)
   - kernel stall
   - scheduler starvation/backpressure

---

## Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)
- Major refactor of model-parallel architecture.
- New comm backend replacement.
- Customer-specific networking/driver remediation (tracked separately by Infra/Private Deploy work).

---

## Scope / workstreams
### A) Scheduler + TP group lifecycle (owner: Sofia Ivanova)
- TP group health model (healthy/degraded/quarantined/resetting)
- Cancellation semantics that cannot deadlock barriers
- Backpressure / load-shedding policies to prevent overload-driven pathologies
- Fairness under mixed sequence lengths (avoid starving long streams or blocking short requests)

### B) Kernels / collectives hardening (owner: Hiro Tanaka)
- Async error checks + propagation strategy (NCCL / collective execution)
- Timeouts on collectives and safe teardown/abort policies
- Stream/event usage hardening to reduce cross-stream deadlocks

### C) Observability + dashboards + alerts (owners: Omar El-Sayed / Allison Grant; implementer: Sergio Costa)
- Per-rank forward progress signals
- Collective latency histograms and “stall signatures” logs
- Dashboard + alert rules with oncall-friendly runbook links

### D) Test & repro harness (owner: Sahana Iyer)
- Deterministic-ish stress suite with fault injection:
  - forced rank delay
  - forced cancel
  - overload patterns (mixed seq lengths, streaming disconnects)
- CI + perf-canary integration with pass/fail criteria

### E) Rollout and operationalization (owner: Rafael Mendes; release coordination: Connor O'Brien)
- Canary plan (Hosted → Dedicated opt-in → default-on)
- Rollback triggers and guardrails
- Dedicated enablement steps + comms templates (w/ Product + Support)

---

## Milestones (target timeline)
**M0: Triage + repro (Week 1–2)**
- Consolidate incident/support evidence + taxonomy of hang signatures
- Add initial instrumentation needed to classify stalls
- First version of repro harness reproducing at least one prod signature

**M1: Core fixes implemented (Week 2–5)**
- Scheduler deadlock/cancellation fixes
- Collective timeout/error propagation hardening
- TP-group watchdog + quarantine behavior (behind flags)

**M2: Validation + canary (Week 5–6)**
- Perf/regression verification gates
- Nightly perf-canary scenarios live + alerting
- Canary in high-load Hosted pools

**M3: Rollout + follow-ups (Week 6–8)**
- Dedicated opt-in + runbook
- Default-on plan agreed per deployment mode
- Close out linked support tickets and postmortem actions

Dates are approximate; final go/no-go is tied to canary results and oncall confidence.

---

## Success metrics / acceptance criteria
- **Repro harness:** no indefinite stalls; watchdog triggers (if any) cause quarantine+reset and do not wedge the worker pool.
- **Hosted canary:** measurable reduction in TP-related timeouts/5xx; watchdog false-positive rate within agreed thresholds.
- **Dedicated:** opt-in customers report resolution or meaningful reduction of hangs; support escalations decline.
- **Oncall:** clear runbook path to identify stall type within 10 minutes using dashboard signals; alerts are actionable (low noise).

---

## Notes on rollout policy (needs PM decision)
We need an explicit decision on default enablement / opt-out per deployment mode:
- Hosted: default-on after canary gates pass
- Dedicated: opt-in first (with recommended thresholds per hardware), then default-on for new clusters
- Private: default-off initially; enable via documented flags with support guidance

Tracked in: PM-513 (policy) and PM-512 (customer comms/release coordination).

---

## Oncall / support coordination
- Support escalation lead: Dev Patel
- SRE guardrails: Rafael Mendes
- Incident commander guidance and paging hygiene to be captured in the runbook + alerts.

---

## Open questions
1) Watchdog sensitivity defaults by hardware (A100/H100/L40S) and by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated) — align with experiments.
2) Abort semantics: when do we fail a single request vs quarantine the entire TP group vs recycle host?
3) How to handle long-lived streams: distinguishing “slow but progressing” vs “stuck” (need robust per-rank progress signal).

---

## Tracking
This umbrella is the coordination point. Please attach updates here when major milestones land (repro, watchdog, canary results, rollout decision). Day-to-day implementation discussion should live on the respective sub-issues.
comments: 2025-02-19 (Noah Patel): Consolidated evidence from Sev1 + recent support escalations. Strongest signal so far is rank skew + missing async error surfacing; scheduling continues to feed a partially wedged group. Next: align on health model + quarantine semantics and ensure we can attribute stalls as comm vs kernel.

2025-02-21 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler fix plan drafted for barrier/cancellation path. Key principle: cancellation must never participate in a barrier that expects all ranks unless we can guarantee all ranks will observe it. Proposing a per-request cancellation epoch and barrier 'lease' with bounded wait + fallback to group quarantine.

2025-02-24 (Hiro Tanaka): Collective hardening in progress. Adding periodic async error checks around long-running collectives, plus clearer propagation up to scheduler so we stop issuing new work. Need to finalize timeout thresholds to avoid false positives on heavy contention.

2025-02-28 (Rafael Mendes): SRE asks that quarantine/reset emits explicit counters with cardinality bounded by tp_group_id only (no request_id in metrics). Alert proposal: page only when resets exceed baseline AND correlated with 5xx/timeouts. Added request for runbook section 'when to shift traffic vs when to drain hosts'.

2025-03-04 (Sahana Iyer): Stress suite now reproduces the streaming-disconnect deadlock signature in staging with fault injection (forced cancel + forced rank delay). Next: wire into nightly perf-canary and define pass/fail (no indefinite stalls; watchdog should recover within N seconds).

2025-03-06 (Connor O'Brien): Targeting runtime-1.19 patch window for first bundled release, but gating on Hosted canary results and false-positive watchdog rate. Please keep PM-512 updated with what’s actually shipping vs behind flags.
